findings.area: Faculty roster / picker / heading nameTags (false positives)
findings.title: nameTags folds every \p{M} after NFKD, so distinct names of scripts where marks are letters get an #id tag as if they were look-alikes: Devanagari "सीता" (#89) and "सता" (#90) both tagged, Hangul compatibility jamo "ㄱㅏ" and the syllable "가" tagged. The tag is harmless (it only adds the student number) but contradicts the server's own rule that marks of other scripts carry meaning. Hangul syllables 김민수/김민서, Braille names, emoji names, fillers (Kim/Kim\u3164Lee/Kim\uffa0Lee, Ola\u115f Nor, Lee\u2800Kim) behave correctly: namesakes tagged, distinct names not
findings.repro: Two students "सीता" and "सता" in one class, open the Faculty roster.
findings.fix_hint: web/src/lib/faculty.ts nameTags fold (line ~154): strip only \p{Mn} of Latin/Greek/Cyrillic/Arabic/Hebrew (as be/src/names.ts does) instead of every \p{M}, and do not NFKD-decompose Hangul.

findings.area: Class-name uniqueness key (classNameKey), residual of R13-A-10
findings.title: Invisible characters are documented as ignored, but a zero-width space BETWEEN TWO SPACES survives: the whitespace collapse runs before the hidden-character removal, so "Biology \u200b 101" (renders like a double space) is a different key from "Biology 101" and is created (201). The picker then shows two identical labels. A trailing Braille blank "Biology 101\u2800" and the Turkish capital "İstanbul A" vs "istanbul a" are also accepted as distinct. Verified refused (409 class_name_taken with details): Cyrillic о, case, double space, ZWSP at either end, ZWSP between letters and spaces, fullwidth, U+3164, soft hyphen, ß/SS, final sigma. Verified distinct on purpose: L1/LI, Section 1.2/12, Year 1/I
findings.actual: 201 and a visually identical twin in the picker.
findings.fix_hint: be/src/names.ts classNameKey (~line 134): remove HIDDEN characters first, then collapse whitespace and trim (and treat U+2800 as a space).

findings.area: Faculty Student detail avatar initialOf with flag emoji
findings.title: A name that starts with a flag ("🇫🇷 Fran", "🇫🇷Fran") gets the avatar "F": regional-indicator pairs are \p{Regional_Indicator}, not \p{Extended_Pictographic}, so the flag grapheme is skipped, while the leaderboard abbreviation of the same student keeps the flag as the initial. Other emoji (family ZWJ sequence, rainbow flag) are kept whole. RLM, ZWSP, soft hyphen, leading combining mark, Braille blank, Hangul filler, punctuation all fall back correctly (R13-C-05 holds)
